chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from a group of my scholars, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) cried over his father, Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), for twenty years or forty years. And whenever food was placed before him, he would cry over Husayn (peace be upon him) until his servant said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I fear that you will be among the perished.' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'I only complain of my distress and grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.' Verily, whenever I remember the killing of the children of Fatimah, I am choked with tears because of it.
ai.seo_question: How long did Imam Sajjad (a.s.) cry for his father Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* illustrates the enduring sorrow of Imam Zayn al-Abidin, whose decades-long weeping for his father was so intense that even food triggered tears, prompting his servant to fear for his health. The Imam’s response, 'I complain of my grief and sorrow to Allah,' directly echoes the Quranic verse of Prophet Yaqub, linking the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering to the prophetic tradition of *bala'* (divine testing) and *sab'r* (patience). This narrative underscores the theological significance of the Ahl al-Bayt's emotional participation in the tragedy of Karbala as a source of spiritual consolation for the Shia community.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father narrated to me from all of my scholars, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

‘Ali ibn Ḥusain (Imam Sajjād (a.s.)) cried over his father, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.), for twenty years – or forty years – and whenever food was brought to him, he would cry over Ḥusain (a.s.). One day his servant said to him, “May I sacrifice myself for you, O son of the Messenger of Allāh! I am afraid that you will die (from grief).” He (Imam Sajjād (a.s.)) replied, “I only complain of my distress and grief to Allāh, and I know from Allāh what you do not know’ [12:86]. Verily whenever I remember the killing of the children of Fāťimah (s.a.), I am choked with tears over them.”
